There are no prizes. Every accepted work is offered for sale at a fixed $100, and sales are split evenly between the artist and the centre, so the artist receives $50 for each work sold.
Delivery is the artist's job. Work is dropped off on Saturday 28 November 2026 and unsold work is collected on Saturday 30 January 2027. Unlike the centre's other calls, this page offers no shipping arrangement.
Applicants email 5–10 images or time-based samples of recent work, an artist statement of 300–500 words, a CV and a short biography, with "Mini Masters" in the subject line. The three 8-inch pieces don't need to be finished at the time of applying. An optional reflection on scale, intimacy or time in the work can be added. The centre says it is looking for originality, craftsmanship and a compelling visual voice, in minimal or layered, narrative or abstract work. — Deadline: November 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artist-in-Residence 2027 · agalab
item.description:
agalab (Amsterdams Grafisch Atelier) is a printmaking workshop in Amsterdam that runs a year-round artist-in-residence programme. It offers six places, two with a guest room beside the workshop and four without accommodation. Residencies run in monthly cycles, from the first Monday to the last Friday of the month, for one to three months, and the 2027 application form lists a cycle for every month of the year.
The residency is self-funded. agalab's own page prices it at €500 a month without accommodation, €1,450 a month with a room (own shower, shared toilets and kitchen, washing machine and dryer, and a bicycle), and €750 for a duo. Materials are not included. Residents pay a €100 downpayment and log their costs on a sheet, and the unused balance is returned at the end. Artists who graduated between 2024 and 2026 can apply for a 50% subsidised place, accommodation not included. Technical introductions beyond the standard ones cost €55 an hour.
Residents have 24/7 access to the workshop. Technicians are on hand Monday to Thursday, silkscreen on Monday and Tuesday, intaglio, relief and lithography on Wednesday and Thursday. Techniques include silkscreen on paper and textile, drypoint and aquatint etching, Toyobo photopolymer plates, stone lithography, linocut, woodcut and letterpress. For photographers, the darkroom has a Durst enlarger, developing tanks for 35mm and 120 film, and a basic stock of developer, stop bath and fixer.
The month has a set shape. Week one brings introductions to the silkscreen and etching workshops, week three a mid-residency studio conversation with the team, a visiting artist and the other residents, and week four an exhibition at agalab's Open Day.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with a reply within about four weeks. The programme is aimed at artists with some printmaking experience, but the page says artists with little or none are also welcome to apply. Applicants email the form with a project plan of up to 120 words, a motivation letter, a CV and a portfolio of up to 20 MB. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: €500–€1,450/month (self-funded). Prize: Residency + Exhibition.

item.title: The Family — Lineage, Choice, and the Album · Der Greif
item.description: A new edition of Der Greif Pulse, the Munich non-profit's online exhibition strand, opened on 22 October 2026 and looking beyond the traditional family portrait. The call addresses family in every form — "whether through bloodline, heritage, or chosen community" — and encourages work on the performance of familial roles and on the deliberate choices behind what gets preserved in the album versus what stays unrecorded. Der Greif names vernacular archive interventions, intimate documentary projects, staged visual narratives and conceptual studies of shared memory among the approaches it wants, and asks what "the family photo" means today. Submit one project of at least 10 images; the conditions of participation state that video is not part of the submission format for this round, and projects previously selected in a Der Greif opportunity should not be re-submitted. Selected artists get an online exhibition in the Pulse section and a place in an online roundtable critique session with peers facilitated by Der Greif staff, plus visibility across the organisation's international community; they may also be invited to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio, which opens routes to artwork sales and commissions. Selection is judged on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with identity and community. Entry is free — Der Greif, a registered non-profit, suggests a voluntary €10 donation and will issue a 50% or 100% discount voucher on request to anyone unable to contribute. The call is international with no age or regional restrictions and is aimed particularly at emerging and mid-career artists. Results are announced in November 2026 and the online exhibition follows in December 2026. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: Free (voluntary €10 donation). Prize: Online exhibition + Group critique session.

item.title: Emergence 2027 · Studio Channel Islands
item.description: Studio Channel Islands Art Center's annual exhibition for students and recent graduates tied to Ventura County, California, running February 6–26, 2027 in the Camarillo gallery. The visual-art application is open to media of every kind — the page states "Open to all media" — and asks for up to six pieces. Eligibility runs on two legs: residents of Ventura County who are currently enrolled at a college or university or graduated from one in the past five years, and non-residents who are currently enrolled at, or graduated in the past five years from, a Ventura County college or university. The jury for the Thomas and Patricia Dodds Award for Excellence picks three winners from the student work — $1,000 for first place and $500 for each of two runners-up — and only artists currently enrolled at a college or university located in Ventura County are eligible for those; a further $1,000 award goes to Best in Show. There is no entry fee. Accepted work must be delivered ready to hang by February 2, 2027 and stay in the gallery until the exhibition closes; sales are split 60% to the artist and 40% to the art center, and the artist sets the price inclusive of that commission. The wider Emergence programme spans visual arts, poetry, film, music and dance, with separate applications on the same page for poetry (also due January 17) and for musicians (due January 6, 2027), and winners of the Dodds award are announced during the February 6 opening reception. — Deadline: January 17, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 + 2×$500 + $1,000 Best in Show.

item.title: Research Fellowships 2027–28 · Center for Creative Photography
item.description: The Center for Creative Photography at the University of Arizona funds research in its Tucson collections and archives. Ten named fellowships are open for the 2027–28 cycle, awarding up to $2,500–$5,000 each. Two are new this year: an Interdisciplinary Research Fellowship (up to $5,000) for research on photographers collaborating with other disciplines, art forms, scientific methods or cultural practices — including new creative projects built on the Center's collections — and the Ilse Sternberg Research Fellowship (up to $4,000) on the history of photographic education. The rest are the Ansel Adams (up to $5,000) and Mickey Pallas (up to $5,000) research fellowships, the Todd Walker (up to $3,500), and the PAC-LA, Harold Jones and Frances Murray, Kenneth J. Botto, Gary Metz and Michael Hawley Artist research fellowships (up to $2,500 each). The Harold Jones and Frances Murray award names curators, historians, social scientists, writers, artists and critics among its applicants, and the Michael Hawley is specifically for a working artist. CCP says it welcomes academic, artistic and public-interest proposals and particularly encourages applicants who bring new and critical approaches to the collections; its published assessment rubric sets out the selection criteria and states that fellowships may support academics, artists or others interested in photographic resources regardless of their experience or educational level. The application form asks whether an applicant will need a visa and notes that CCP funds visas for visiting researchers. The Adolf Fassbender Travel Fellowship is not offered in this cycle. Applications close 19 January 2027 at 11:59pm MST, and the form says applicants are notified in early March. — Deadline: January 19, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Research fellowship + $2,500–$5,000 award.

item.title: Love Is … 2027 National Show · Northern California Arts, Inc.
item.description: Northern California Arts, Inc.'s first edition of this national all-media juried show, held at the Sacramento Fine Arts Center in Carmichael, California. Artists define “love” however they wish — the prospectus names love of nature, romantic love and parental love as examples — and says the show is otherwise open to all artworks, though the NCA board may deny entry to work it judges to hold unacceptable subject matter (its example is graphic violence). Open to artists 18 or older residing in the USA; photography, collage and mixed media are explicitly listed among the accepted media, and printed media is allowed only for photography. Up to three works, each no more than three years old and not previously shown at Sacramento Fine Arts; AI-made work is barred. Entry is $25 per work for non-members ($20 for NCA members), or $60 for three works ($50 for members). Judged by Suzy Goodwin, who assigns a Best of Show and category awards; the award amounts are not published in the prospectus. Sacramento Fine Arts handles all sales and takes a 30% commission from members and 50% from non-members, and remote artists pay shipping both ways plus a crating fee of $25 for one piece or $30 for two. Exhibition January 26 – February 13, 2027. — Deadline: January 3, 2027. Fee: $25 per work ($20 members); 3 works $60 ($50 members). Prize: Group exhibition + Best of Show and category awards.

item.title: Our Planet 2026: Nature, Landscape and Conservation · Atlanta Photography Group
item.description: Atlanta Photography Group's winter 2026 juried show takes work on nature, landscape, environmentalism and conservation — flora, fauna, nature-based documentary and fine art, and work about animals, insects, reptiles and fish and their habitat. The juror is Alex Snyder, Senior Photo Editor at The Nature Conservancy, a photo editor and photojournalist who has produced more than thirty features for Nature Conservancy Magazine, serves as Communications Director for The Photo Society (the collective of over 200 National Geographic photographers), and was named Photo Editor of the Year National by the NPPA's Best of Photojournalism awards in 2025. Selected work hangs in the APG Gallery at Ansley Mall in Atlanta from 15 December 2026 to 22 January 2027, with an opening reception on 17 December. Submission is open to current APG members only, and membership can be bought or renewed at the point of entry. The fee ladder is tiered by date and by image count: up to five images costs $35 at the early deadline of 23 October, $40 at the regular deadline of 2 November and $50 at the late deadline of 6 November, with each additional image $6 up to ten total; students enrolled in a degree or certificate programme start at $20. CAUTION on the student rate: the printed table on APG’s own page says $4 per additional image, but the purchase options on that same page price every student step at $6 — $20 for up to five images, then $26, $32, $38, $44 and $50 for ten — so budget from the checkout options, not from the table. Accepted prints may be up to 36 inches on the longest side, framed, and must reach the gallery by 11 December. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $35–$80 (members) / $20–$50 (students). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals · New Bedford Art Museum
item.description: New Bedford Art Museum takes exhibition proposals on a rolling basis from artists, independent curators, scholars, partner institutions and community members, with its exhibition committee reviewing submissions quarterly. The museum plans two to five years ahead, so this is a long-horizon route into a programme that takes photography seriously without being a photography programme: its 2026 group show Vanishing Ecologies: Speculative Futures lists photography among the media it brings together, and the two juried calls the museum has run that we track both name photography among accepted work — in each case alongside every other visual medium, not on its own. There is no fee and no theme; a proposal goes to the Executive Director by email and must explain how the exhibition fulfils the museum's mission, supply a checklist of the artworks with sample images, titles, media and a proposed gallery layout, describe the theme and its influences, propose display timing, list related talks or workshops, and give a timeline. CAUTION on the money: the museum asks each proposal to include a budget covering shipping, installation and de-installation and reception expenses, plus proposed sponsorship partners and a publicity plan - the page names no stipend or production fund, so clarify who pays for what before committing. Curators are told not to include their own work in a proposal. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: Winter Open Call · Flow Space Gallery
item.description: Flow Space Gallery, a Chelsea gallery at 526 W 26th Street, is taking submissions for its Winter open call, looking for emerging and mid-career artists who identify as women or queer for solo and group shows. Artists working in all mediums are encouraged to apply and photography is named explicitly in the presentation rules — works on paper and photographs must arrive framed and ready to hang. All work submitted is considered for future exhibition opportunities rather than one fixed show, so the gallery treats the call as an ongoing route into its programme. Applications go through a Google Form carrying a PDF of five to ten images with material, dimensions, year, title and price for each, plus an artist statement, bio and CV, and a screenshot of the $20 submission payment. The gallery states plainly that it is a small team and only accepted artists will be contacted, and that unsolicited applications outside this process are not accepted. Shipping work to the gallery is the artist's responsibility. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Pearl Press — Solo Issue Open Call
item.description: Pearl Press is an independent online publication, 28 issues deep, that normally runs themed group issues. The next one is different: the whole issue goes to a single photographer, or to a collaboration between two. The call asks for 20 to 30 pieces with a one-page bio and a description of the work, and sets no theme at all — 'there is no concept to adhere to', so the brief is simply a body of work you are proud of. The selected artist is interviewed inside the issue (both photographers, where two apply together) and promoted on the publication's Instagram. Submission is free and by email, with visual work at a minimum of 300 dpi; more than 30 pieces may be sent, though only part of what arrives will be used. The publication was founded by Delilah Twersky, a fine-arts photographer and creative writer who works primarily with medium-format film and whose own work has been published by Dashwood Books, Waif Magazine, Aint-Bad and Sissy Screens; Pearl Press itself has been interviewed by Chill Subs. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo issue publication with interview.

item.title: 2027 Student Showcase · Gresham Area League for the Arts
item.description: The Gresham Area League for the Arts' student show, hung in GALA's gallery in the Gresham City Council Chambers, Oregon, from 11 January to 19 February 2027 and opened with an artists' reception and award ceremony on 14 January. GALA invites students in grades 6 through 12 from the East County school districts and surrounding areas, and names photography directly alongside ceramics, digital art, drawing, fibre, glass, metalwork, mixed media, painting, printmaking, sculpture and wood; 2D and 3D work are both welcome. Reproducible work — computer-generated art, digitally altered photographs, giclee prints — must be labelled as such, and photographic prints must be signed, numbered as part of a limited edition and meet archival standards. Work must be entirely the student's own and made within the last year: no class step-out pieces, no paint-by-number. The gallery lends frames in four sizes (12x16, 12x18, 16x20 and 14x14) to students who need them and retains 20% commission on sales; submissions must stay clear of nudity, sexual content and divisive themes for a family-friendly multi-use space. Accepted work is delivered in person on 8 or 9 January and stays up for the whole run, with an art talk on 4 February and an education Saturday on 6 February. No entry fee is stated anywhere on the call page. Entries close at midnight on Wednesday 16 December 2026. — Deadline: December 16, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Portrait Series Open Call · SHOW LA
item.description: SHOW LA — the Los Angeles photography fair that runs 10–13 December 2026 at The Reef, 1933 S. Broadway — has partnered with LensCulture on an open call for portrait photography. Photographers of all categories and levels may submit a portrait series of up to ten images, which should sit within the same body of work or series; entries opened 6 October and close 30 October. The grand prize winner takes a $1,000 cash prize, a feature on SHOW LA's Instagram account and an exhibition at SHOW LA this December; three finalists are exhibited at the fair alongside the winner. The call is open internationally and is judged by three jurors — Paris Chong, gallery director of the Leica Store & Gallery Los Angeles, Ann M. Jastrab, executive director of the Center for Photographic Art, and Matthew Martin, director of the Peter Fetterman Gallery. Entry is $45 and submissions are handled on LensCulture, whose entry route requires a signed-in account. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: $1,000 + exhibition at SHOW LA.

item.title: BROAD Magazine — Open Submissions
item.description: Independent visual-culture photography publication that features one photographer's project at a time on its website, with a short artist text alongside the pictures — recent features include Giovanni Fafoglia's Cellophane, Federica Nannini's Assenze silenziose on emptied high-school classrooms, Roberto Zeppilli's Fotosottocasa made entirely within walking distance of his home, and Sinziana Velicescu's Purgatory, Paradise on civic and commercial architecture across the American landscape. BROAD describes itself as a community-driven publication working with artists from around the world and says it is always open to submissions: there is no theme, no deadline and no fee on this route. Applicants fill in the form on the submissions page and supply a direct link to a gallery or folder of the images they want considered (Dropbox or Google Drive both fine). Because of the volume received, BROAD contacts photographers only if their submission is selected for publication. Note that BROAD's separate themed print issues run as their own open calls with their own paid community-membership route; this rolling route is for the website features. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: What the Streets Hold · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Decagon Gallery's Spotlight open call for street photography, juried by the gallery's own Curator and Artistic Director, Teona Machavariani. The brief is about what people reveal without intending to — how they wait, protect themselves, occupy space, move toward one another, or remain separate while standing side by side — and the gallery is explicit that it is not after dramatic events, visual coincidences or perfectly timed gestures, but photographs that make you pause because something in them feels known even when you cannot explain what happened. Work may be made on streets, in stations, markets, public transport, neighbourhoods or anywhere strangers temporarily share a place; a person can be central, barely visible, or present only through what they have left behind. All photographic processes and styles are welcome, open to photographers worldwide over 18. Awards total $1,000 — $500 first place, $250 second, $150 third and two $50 honourable mentions, one cash award per photographer — plus a Human Presence Award giving free entry to a future Decagon exhibition. Selected artists get an online exhibition, publication in a professionally designed exhibition catalog, and digital badges and certificates. Photographers retain all rights including copyright; the gallery takes the right to publish selected work in the exhibition, the catalog and promotion. Entry is $25 for up to four photographs and $5 for each additional, and the entry form carries ten upload slots. Exhibition runs February 10 – April 10, 2027. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $25 (4 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $1,000 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: FOTODOKS Open Call 2027
item.description: FOTODOKS, the biennial festival for contemporary documentary photography in Munich, is building the central group exhibition of its thirteenth edition (October 2027) from an open call on care — care as emotional, physical, psychological, social and relational work, and its entanglement with politics, labour, ethics and intimate relationships at a moment when 'community' and 'belonging' circulate as branded buzzwords. The festival seeks existing lens-based, documentary-driven stories of care with a photorealistic and honest intention, asking how documentary photography meets today's imaginaries of care after the dismantling of welfare-state models and the rise of 'self-care' as a slogan for overworked bodies. Submit one project of 5-10 images, in English or German; individuals, duos and collectives are all eligible, and the curatorial team also extends direct invitations alongside the open call. Selected artists receive an artist fee of EUR 500 (EUR 800 for duos, up to EUR 1,200 for collectives), a travel budget of up to EUR 150 within Germany, EUR 300 within Europe or EUR 500 from outside Europe, accommodation for the four-day opening week, full production of the work for the exhibition, inclusion in the festival catalogue with five printed copies, and a presentation on the FOTODOKS website. FOTODOKS encourages applicants of all ethnic backgrounds, religions, ages, genders, disabilities, sexual orientations and social statuses, does not sell exhibited work, and leaves copyright with the artist. Results early spring 2027. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 artist fee + Exhibition.

item.title: SPACE: Exterus Spatium · Crooked Tree Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition in the Carnegie and Cornwell Galleries at Crooked Tree Arts Center in Traverse City, Michigan, on outer space: the moon, the planets, the stars, solar systems, galaxies and beyond, or their effects on our Earth. Science fact and science fiction are equally encouraged, and work may be literal or abstract, traditional or experimental, miniature or monumental. All media are welcome except AI; photography and telescopic images are eligible as long as the image was solely captured and reproduced by the artist. Open to US residents 18+, up to three works completed within the last three years. $30 entry, $20 for CTAC members, free for Guild members. Notification 4 December 2026; exhibition 15 January - 27 February 2027. The galleries are sales galleries and CTAC retains a 40% commission on sales; work need not be for sale. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $30 ($20 members). Prize: Exhibition.
